EXPLORATORY DATA ANALYSIS ON Programmers Survey

PROBLEM STATEMENT:

The Goal of this Project is to analyze the Stack overflow Developer Survey data to understand developer demographics, employment, patterns and work trends using exploratory data analysis(EDA).

Project Flow Section

1.Data loading and cleaning
2.Exploratory data analysis
3.Visualization of key patterns
4.Insights and conclusions

Why This Analysis Need:

Understanding developer demographics, employment patterns, and work habits to help organizations to better analysis.
Design better hiring strategies and improve developer work-life balance and generated Analysis on this Dataset.

Data Cleaning Decisions

*Removed null values from key columns like (Age, Employment, Country,Job Factor) etc.,
*Standarized categorical values for consistency.
*Dropped irrelevant columns to reduce noise and unneccessary data.

SUMMARY

This Project analyzes the Stack Overflow Developer Survey dataset to understand global developer demographics,employment,patterns,education backgrounds,and work habits. Using Python,Pandas,Numpy,Matplotlib&Seaborn and key insights were extracted through exploratory data analysis and visualization.

STEP-1.SELECT A REAL-WORLD DATASET

*Find and download an interesting real-world dataset from Internet KAGGLE(Recommended). *The dataset should contain tabular data (rows&columns),Prefer in CSV,JSON,XLS or other formats that can read using pandas. *If its not compatible format, you may have to write some code to convert it to desired formart. *The dataset should contain at least 3 columns and 150 rows of data. This is minimum dataset to show case the formulas exploration.

STEP-2.PERFORM DATA PREPARATION & CLEANING

Load the dataset into a data frame using Pandas.Explore the total number of rows & columns,ranges of values etc. *Handle missing, incorrect and invalid data from the dataset. *Perform any additional steps if needed (like creating additonal columns for the dataset, merging dataset etc).

STEP-3.PERFORM EXPLORATORY ANALYSIS & VISUALIZATION

Compute the mean,sum,range and other intresting statistics for numeric columns.Explore distributions of numeric columns using histograms.*Explore relationship between columns using bar charts, scatter plots. *Make a note of interesting insights from the exploratory analysis.

STEP-4.ASK & ANSWER QUESTIONS ABOUT THE DATA

Ask at least 5 interesting questions about your dataset. Answer the questions either by computing the results using Numpy/Pandas or by Plotting graphs using Matplotlib/Seaborn.*create new coloumns,merge mulitple dataset and perform grouping/aggregation wherever necessary.***Mainly wherever you are using library functions from Pandas/Numpy/Matplotlib/Seaborn first import them correctly then use it.

STEP-5.SUMMARIZE YOUR INFERENECES & WRITE A CONCLUSION

*Write a summary of what you learned from the analysis,inlcuding interesting insights and graphs from your notebook make to SAVE IT to share with other people.

STEP-6.SHARE TO GITHUB REPOSITORY TO STORE YOUR INFO OF YOUR COMPLETE PROJECT

In [97]:
DevType = "DevType"
In [98]:
def split_multicolumn(survey_df, col):
    result_df = survey_df.copy()
    options = []
    #Iterate over the column
    for idx, value in survey_df[col].dropna().items():
        #Break each value into list of options
        for option in value.split(';'):
            #Add the option as a common to result
            if not option in result_df.columns:
                result_df[option] = False
                options.append(option)
                #Mark the value in the option column as True
            result_df.at[idx, option] = True
        return result_df[options]

INFERENCES AND CONCLUSIONS

We've drawn many interesting inferences from the survey, here's a summary of the few of them:

Based on the demographics of the survey respondents, we can infer that the survey is somewhat representative of the overall programming community, although it definitely has fewer responses from programmers in non-English-speaking countries and from women & non-binary genders.

The programming community is not as diverse as it can be, and although things are improving, we should take more efforts to support & encourage members of underrepresented communities -whether it is in terms of age, country, race, gender or otherwise.

Most programmers hold a college degree, although a fairly large percentage did not have computer science as their major in college, so a computer science degree isn't compulsory for learning to code or building a career in programming.

A significant percentage of programmers either work part time or as freelancers, and this can be a great way to break into the field, especially when you're just getting started.

Javascript & HTML/CSS are the most used programming languages in 2020, closely followed by SQL & Python

Python is the language most people are interested in learning - since it is an easy-to-learn general purpose programming language well suited for a variety of domains.

Rust and TypeScript are the most "loved" languages in 2020, both of which have small but fast-growing communities. Python is a close third, despite already being a widely used language.

Programmers around the world seems be working for around 40 hours a week on average, with slight variations by country.

Finally: You can learn and start programming professionally at any age, and you're likely to have a long and fulfilling career if you also enjoy programming as a hobby.

REFERENCES AND FUTURE WORK

There's a wealth of information to be discovered using the survey, and we've barely scratched the surface. Here are some ideas for further exploration:

Analyze salary trends by country and experience

Compare results with previous survey years

Prepare an analysis focusing on diversity - and identify areas where underrepresented communities are with the majority (e.g. education) and where they aren't (e.g. salaries)

Compare the results of this year's survey with the previous years and identify interesting trends
